statement: Fenestrated capillaries have:

options.b: a thickened endothelium containing large gaps.
options.c: an altered basement membrane with broad clefts.
options.d: extremely attenuated areas of endothelium with pores.
options.e: pores that are evenly spaced over the entire surface.

explanation.d: Fenestrated capillaries are characterized by extremely attenuated areas of endothelium with pores that span the thin cytoplasm of the endothelial cells.
explanation.a: A discontinuous basal lamina is a defining structural feature of sinusoidal capillaries, not fenestrated capillaries.
explanation.b: The endothelium of fenestrated capillaries is highly thinned and attenuated, not a thickened endothelium containing large gaps.
explanation.c: They possess a continuous and structurally intact basement membrane rather than an altered basement membrane with broad clefts.
explanation.e: The pores are organized in clustered patches or fenestrated fields rather than being pores that are evenly spaced over the entire surface.

subject: Histology

statement: When compared to arteries, veins have each of the following characteristics except:

options.c: less developed muscle in tunica media.
options.d: less developed elastic tissue in tunica media.
options.e: the adventitia is often the thickest layer.

explanation.a: This statement is false because veins operate under low-pressure conditions and contain a noticeably low amount of elastic fibers compared to high-pressure arteries.
explanation.b: It is true that veins display a larger caliber and thinner walls than their companion arteries due to lower structural resistance demands.
explanation.c: It is true that veins have a less developed muscle in tunica media, exhibiting fewer and more loosely organized smooth muscle strands.
explanation.d: It is true that veins feature less developed elastic tissue in tunica media, lacking distinct, highly consolidated elastic lamellae.
explanation.e: It is true that the adventitia is often the thickest layer in venous walls, composed primarily of collagenous connective tissue.

subject: Histology

statement: The vessels whose adventitia is described as thick longitudinal bundles of collagen and elastic fibers and isolated longitudinal bundles of smooth muscle are:

explanation.e: Large venules and medium-to-large veins characteristically display a thick tunica adventitia containing longitudinal bundles of collagen, elastic fibers, and isolated longitudinal bundles of smooth muscle.
explanation.a: Arterioles are small, regulatory resistance vessels that completely lack longitudinal bundles of smooth muscle within their thin outer adventitial layer.
explanation.b: Capillaries are minimal microscopic exchange channels composed solely of endothelium and a basal lamina, entirely lacking an adventitia.
explanation.c: Elastic arteries possess a thin tunica adventitia composed of loose connective tissue, with a tunica media dominated by concentric, circular elastic lamellae.
explanation.d: Muscular arteries feature an adventitia composed of dense collagen and elastic fibers, completely lacking isolated longitudinal bundles of smooth muscle cells.

subject: Histology

statement: Which of the following statements about healthy, intact capillaries is true:

options.c: They are lined by a simple columnar epithelium.
options.d: They have a continuous smooth muscle coat.
options.e: They possess a thick tunica adventitia.

explanation.b: Healthy, intact capillaries secrete antithrombotic factors like prostacyclin and nitric oxide to inhibit intravascular clot formation along their luminal surface.
explanation.a: Systemic blood pressure is controlled and adjusted by the tone of muscular arterioles rather than by individual capillaries.
explanation.c: Capillaries are lined by a simple squamous epithelium (endothelium), not by a simple columnar epithelium.
explanation.d: Capillaries are completely devoid of smooth muscle, lacking a continuous smooth muscle coat entirely within their thin exchange walls.
explanation.e: Capillaries consist only of an endothelial tube and a basal lamina, meaning they completely lack a thick tunica adventitia.

subject: Histology

statement: Diameter of Sinusoidal Capillaries:

explanation.b: The diameter of Sinusoidal Capillaries characteristically ranges between 30–40 microns, providing an enlarged, slow-flowing luminal pathway that optimizes cellular and molecular exchange.
explanation.a: A diameter of 10–20 microns corresponds to the luminal size of standard continuous capillaries, fenestrated capillaries, or small postcapillary venules.
explanation.c: A span of 50–60 microns exceeds the normal physiological diameter of sinusoidal channels in lymphoid, hepatic, and hematopoietic organs.
explanation.d: A range of 60–80 microns represents larger venular structures or small collecting veins rather than individual sinusoidal capillary beds.
explanation.e: A diameter of 90–100 microns defines macroscopic venous channels and small veins, far exceeding the scale of microvascular sinusoidal networks.

subject: Histology

statement: Regulation of the size of the lumen of bronchioles is controlled by:

explanation.d: Bronchioles lack structural cartilage, meaning dynamic luminal diameter regulation relies entirely on the constriction/relaxation of smooth muscle countered by the radial traction of elastic fibers.
explanation.a: Cartilage is structurally absent in bronchioles, meaning elastic fibers alone cannot actively regulate or contract the lumen.
explanation.b: Hyaline cartilage plates are structural features characteristic of bronchi and are entirely lost by the time the airway transitions into a bronchiole.
explanation.c: Collagen provides passive structural tensile strength to the airway wall but lacks the high elasticity required to structurally balance active smooth muscle luminal regulation.
explanation.e: Hyaline cartilage is not found within bronchiolar walls, rendering options reliant on cartilage mechanics invalid for this airway segment.

subject: Histology

statement: A medical student while examining the slide of a terminal bronchiole found a dome-shaped cell with extensive RER, well developed Golgi complex, abundant mitochondria and some profiles of SER. The cell is?

explanation.c: Clara cell (exocrine bronchiolar cell) is a non-ciliated, dome-shaped cell residing in bronchioles, ultrastructurally optimized with extensive RER, well developed Golgi complex, and SER profiles to secrete surfactant-like proteins and detoxify xenobiotics.
explanation.a: Basal cell is a short, triangular stem cell resting on the basement membrane of larger conducting airways, lacking a dome-shaped apical profile.
explanation.b: Brush cell is characterized by specialized apical microvilli and a chemosensory role rather than a dense secretory ultrastructure.
explanation.d: Goblet cell is a mucus-secreting cell containing large, pale apical mucin granules instead of a dome-shaped profile packed with diverse metabolic organelles.
explanation.e: Kulchitsky cell is an enteroendocrine cell filled with small dense-core granules near its basal aspect to secrete amine hormones into the lamina propria.

subject: Histology

statement: Multi-lamellar bodies are present in?

explanation.e: Type II pneumocytes contain multi-lamellar bodies, which are specialized, membrane-bound intracellular storage granules packed with concentric whorls of newly synthesized surfactant phospholipids.
explanation.a: Alveolar macrophages contain heterophagic lysosomes and phagosomes containing engulfed debris, not secretory multi-lamellar bodies.
explanation.b: Bronchiolar brush cells contain chemosensory elements and glycogen stores, but lack surfactant-storing multi-lamellar bodies.
explanation.c: Exocrine bronchiolar cells (Clara cells) contain dense, electron-opaque apical secretory granules, not multi-lamellar structures.
explanation.d: Type I pneumocytes possess minimal organelles within their thin cytoplasm and do not synthesize or store material in multi-lamellar bodies.

subject: Histology

statement: Which type of junctions present between type I pneumocytes and type II pneumocytes?

explanation.e: Occluding junctions (tight junctions) seal the intercellular spaces between adjacent Type I and Type II pneumocytes, preventing the unregulated paracellular leakage of interstitial fluid into the alveolar air spaces.
explanation.a: Anchoring junctions mechanically attach cells to the matrix or cytoskeleton but do not form a tight physical seal against fluid transudation.
explanation.b: Communicating junctions allow direct cytoplasmic transfer of small signaling ions between adjacent cells but do not seal extracellular spaces.
explanation.c: Desmosomal junctions provide strong localized spot adhesion to resist mechanical shearing forces but do not form a continuous occluding barrier.
explanation.d: Gap junctions allow metabolic and electrical coupling via connexons but are structural variants of communicating junctions, not sealing junctions.

subject: Histology

statement: Which of the following components increase(s) as a proportion of the respiratory tract wall from trachea to alveoli?

explanation.b: Elastic fibers increase in relative proportion as the airway descends, forming a vital continuous structural network that drives passive elastic recoil during expiration.
explanation.a: Cilia decrease in density and height from the trachea downward, disappearing completely before the air reaches the alveoli.
explanation.d: Seromucous glands are confined to the submucosa of the trachea and bronchi, disappearing completely at the bronchiolar level.
explanation.c: Hyaline cartilage decreases progressively down the bronchial tree and is entirely absent past the small bronchi, failing to reach the alveoli.
explanation.e: Smooth muscle increases proportionally through the bronchioles but drops off rapidly, becoming highly sparse and discontinuous in alveolar walls.

subject: Histology

statement: Which of the following features distinguishes a bronchus within a lung from the primary bronchus?

explanation.b: Intrapulmonary bronchi contain irregular plates of hyaline cartilage, whereas the extrapulmonary primary bronchus retains the continuous C-shaped rings characteristic of the trachea.
explanation.a: Glands in the submucosa are found in both primary and intrapulmonary bronchi, so they cannot serve as a distinguishing feature between them.
explanation.c: Pseudostratified ciliated columnar epithelium lines the lumina of both primary and larger intrapulmonary bronchi, making it non-diagnostic.
explanation.d: Smooth muscle in the wall is organized into a prominent interlacing spiral layer in both structures to regulate airway diameter.
explanation.e: Thick connective tissue adventitia blends into surrounding structures in both bronchial regions, failing to serve as a reliable microscopic differentiator.

subject: Histology

statement: All the following about the olfactory epithelium are true EXCEPT:

options.a: basal cells rest on Descemet’s membrane.
options.d: the lamina propria contains unmyelinated axons.

explanation.a: Basal cells rest on a standard epithelial basement membrane, whereas Descemet’s membrane is a specialized basement membrane located exclusively in the cornea of the eye.
explanation.b: Bowman's glands are present underneath the epithelium in the lamina propria, where they produce a serous fluid to dissolve odorants.
explanation.c: Sustentacular cells have prominent microvilli on their apical surfaces to support olfactory cilia and maintain the ionic microenvironment.
explanation.d: The lamina propria contains unmyelinated axons originating from olfactory receptor neurons that coalesce to form the olfactory nerve fascicles.
explanation.e: The neuro-epithelium have olfactory vesicles, which are the bulbous apical terminations of olfactory neurons from which non-motile cilia project.

subject: Histology

statement: When IgE on a mast cell Fcε receptor is cross linked by an allergen, the mast cell responds by:

explanation.b: Cross-linking of IgE bound to Fcε receptors triggers mast-cell degranulation with rapid release of histamine.
explanation.a: Mast cells are not the principal antigen-presenting cells for Th-cell activation.
explanation.c: IgE is produced by plasma cells, not mast cells.
explanation.d: Complement proteins are synthesized mainly by hepatocytes rather than mast cells.
explanation.e: Allergen-mediated activation causes degranulation, not apoptosis.

subject: Pathology

statement: Which one of the following is associated with increased lung compliance:

explanation.a: Emphysema increases lung compliance because alveolar wall destruction reduces elastic recoil.
explanation.b: Kyphosis restricts chest wall expansion and decreases overall compliance.
explanation.c: Pleural fibrosis stiffens the lungs and chest wall.
explanation.d: Pulmonary edema reduces compliance by filling alveoli with fluid.
explanation.e: Pulmonary fibrosis markedly decreases lung compliance.

subject: Pathology

statement: Bronchogenic carcinoma has increased incidence in pneumoconiosis. Most likely association is with:

explanation.a: Asbestosis markedly increases the risk of bronchogenic carcinoma, especially in smokers.
explanation.b: Bagassosis is a hypersensitivity pneumonitis without a strong carcinoma association.
explanation.c: Berylliosis is mainly associated with granulomatous lung disease.
explanation.d: Silicosis has a stronger association with tuberculosis than bronchogenic carcinoma.
explanation.e: Talcosis is not classically linked to bronchogenic carcinoma.

subject: Pathology

statement: In the pathogenesis of bronchiectasis, susceptibility to infection is due to:

options.a: accumulation of thick and viscid secretions obstructing airways.

explanation.a: Accumulation of thick and viscid secretions obstructing airways impairs clearance and promotes recurrent infection.
explanation.b: Epithelial sloughing is largely a consequence rather than the primary cause of susceptibility.
explanation.c: Immunodeficient status may predispose but is not the general mechanism described.
explanation.d: Progressive fibrosis of lung parenchyma is not the key initiating factor.
explanation.e: Smooth muscle hypertrophy does not explain recurrent infection.

subject: Pathology

statement: Question: Because of its anti-inflammatory mechanism of action, which drug requires regular administration for the treatment of asthma?

explanation.b: Inhaled fluticasone must be taken regularly to suppress chronic airway inflammation.
explanation.a: Inhaled albuterol is used as needed for symptom relief.
explanation.c: Inhaled ipratropium mainly provides bronchodilation.
explanation.d: Oral theophylline is primarily a bronchodilator.
explanation.e: Oral zafirlukast is anti-inflammatory but inhaled corticosteroids remain the cornerstone requiring regular administration.

subject: Pharmacology

statement: Question: Which of the following, in its parenteral form, is lifesaving in severe status asthmaticus?

explanation.b: Parenteral epinephrine produces rapid bronchodilation and can be lifesaving in severe status asthmaticus.
explanation.a: Aminophylline has a slower and less predictable effect.
explanation.c: Isoproterenol is rarely used because of significant cardiac adverse effects.
explanation.d: Terbutaline may be useful but is not the classic lifesaving parenteral drug.
explanation.e: Theophylline is not first-line emergency therapy.

subject: Pharmacology

statement: Question: All of the following statements regarding the use of glucocorticoids in asthma are true except:

options.a: They are administered as prophylactic medications.
options.b: They are often combined with β2-agonists.
options.c: They have a delayed onset of action.
options.d: They reduce bronchial inflammation and hyperreactivity.

explanation.e: Glucocorticoids do not produce direct bronchodilation; they act by reducing inflammation.
explanation.a: They are widely used as prophylactic medications.
explanation.b: Combination with β2-agonists is standard asthma therapy.
explanation.c: Their clinical benefits develop gradually due to genomic effects.
explanation.d: They effectively reduce bronchial inflammation and hyperreactivity.

subject: Pharmacology

statement: Question: A child with asthma is to be treated with a drug that blocks the synthesis of leukotrienes. Which drug is the most appropriate choice?

explanation.e: Zileuton inhibits 5-lipoxygenase, thereby blocking the synthesis of leukotrienes.
explanation.a: Cromolyn sodium stabilizes mast cells.
explanation.b: Montelukast blocks leukotriene receptors rather than synthesis.
explanation.c: Theophylline is a methylxanthine bronchodilator.
explanation.d: Zafirlukast is a leukotriene receptor antagonist.

subject: Pharmacology

statement: Question: Which of the following has a slow onset, long duration of action, and should always be used in combination with an inhaled corticosteroid?

explanation.e: Salmeterol is a long-acting β2-agonist that should be combined with an inhaled corticosteroid in asthma.
explanation.a: Aminophylline is a methylxanthine, not a LABA.
explanation.b: Epinephrine is a short-acting emergency bronchodilator.
explanation.c: Formoterol has a more rapid onset than salmeterol.
explanation.d: Ipratropium is an antimuscarinic bronchodilator.

subject: Pharmacology

statement: Question: Which of the following is not an established prophylactic strategy for asthma?

explanation.b: Blockade of histamine receptors has limited efficacy and is not an established prophylactic strategy for asthma.
explanation.a: Avoidance of antigen exposure reduces trigger-induced attacks.
explanation.c: Blockade of leukotriene receptors is an accepted preventive approach.
explanation.d: Inhibition of phospholipase A2 decreases inflammatory mediator production.
explanation.e: Suppression of airway inflammation is a central preventive strategy.

subject: Pharmacology

statement: Question: All of the following combinations of drug and mechanism of action are correct except:

options.a: Salbutamol: stimulation of β2 receptors causing bronchodilation
options.c: Theophylline: non-selective β2 receptor stimulation causing bronchodilation

explanation.c: Theophylline does not cause non-selective β2 receptor stimulation; it acts mainly through phosphodiesterase inhibition and adenosine receptor antagonism.
explanation.a: Salbutamol stimulates β2 receptors causing bronchodilation.
explanation.b: Sodium cromoglycate acts through mast cell stabilization.
explanation.d: Zafirlukast blocks leukotriene receptors.
explanation.e: Zileuton inhibits leukotriene synthesis by blocking 5-lipoxygenase.

subject: Pharmacology

statement: Question: Which of the following inhibits acetylcholine-mediated bronchospasm?

explanation.b: Ipratropium blocks muscarinic receptors and prevents acetylcholine-mediated bronchospasm.
explanation.a: Ephedrine acts primarily through adrenergic stimulation.
explanation.c: Salmeterol causes bronchodilation via β2 receptor activation.
explanation.d: Theophylline acts through phosphodiesterase inhibition and adenosine receptor antagonism.
explanation.e: Terbutaline is a selective β2-agonist bronchodilator.

subject: Pharmacology

statement: A 32-year-old pilot complains of seasonal allergies. Which medication is most appropriate for management of his allergy symptoms:

explanation.d: fexofenadine is a second-generation H1 antihistamine with minimal sedation, making it ideal for pilots requiring alertness.
explanation.a: cetirizine may still cause mild sedation compared to fexofenadine.
explanation.b: cyclizine is primarily an antiemetic for motion sickness, not allergic rhinitis.
explanation.c: diphenhydramine is a first-generation antihistamine causing significant sedation.
explanation.e: promethazine is highly sedating and unsuitable for tasks requiring wakefulness.

subject: Pharmacology

statement: Which of the following drugs is the most effective physiologic antagonist of histamine in smooth muscle:

explanation.c: epinephrine physiologically reverses histamine effects via α- and β-adrenergic stimulation in smooth muscle.

statement: A patient suffers from troublesome allergic rhinitis due to pollen, and you want to prescribe a drug that is least likely to cause sedation. What is your best choice:

explanation.d: hydroxyzine is a sedating first-generation antihistamine.

statement: Antihistamines are used in all of the following except:

explanation.d: antihistamines are not primarily indicated for inducing sleep therapeutically.

explanation.c: hay fever is a standard indication for H1 blockers.

options.a: because of long-term safety first generation drugs are first choice

subject: Physiology

statement: A person shifts from Peshawar to an area of Swat valley about 10,000 feet above sea level. Which physiological change increases most rapidly to resist hypoxia?

explanation.a: Arterial chemoreceptor activity increases immediately, driving hyperventilation to counter hypoxia.
explanation.b: Growth of systemic capillaries occurs slowly over weeks, not rapidly.
explanation.c: Pulmonary diffusing capacity improves gradually, not acutely.
explanation.d: RBC formation requires days to weeks via erythropoietin stimulation.
explanation.e: Ventricular hypertrophy develops only in chronic hypoxic stress, not rapidly.

subject: Physiology

statement: At high altitudes?

options.a: Chemoreceptors become more sensitive to CO₂
options.b: Chemoreceptors become more sensitive to H⁺
options.c: Chemoreceptors become more sensitive to O₂
options.d: Chemoreceptors become more sensitive to O₂, CO₂ and H⁺
options.e: Chemoreceptors become less sensitive to O₂

explanation.a: Chemoreceptors become more sensitive to CO₂, enhancing ventilatory drive under hypoxia.
explanation.b: Sensitivity to H⁺ does not increase significantly at altitude.
explanation.c: Sensitivity to O₂ is already high but does not increase further.
explanation.d: Combined sensitivity to O₂, CO₂ and H⁺ is not uniformly enhanced.
explanation.e: Chemoreceptors do not become less sensitive to O₂; hypoxia heightens their role.

subject: Physiology

statement: Which of the following is a common cause of hypercapnia?

explanation.b: Hypoventilation reduces CO₂ clearance, leading to hypercapnia.
explanation.a: Hyperventilation lowers CO₂, causing hypocapnia.
explanation.c: Increased oxygen delivery does not affect CO₂ retention.
explanation.d: Increased oxygen saturation of Hb does not alter CO₂ elimination.
explanation.e: Reduced metabolic rate decreases CO₂ production, not increases it.

subject: Physiology

statement: If a person goes to high altitude, it will lead to?

explanation.d: Respiratory alkalosis occurs due to hyperventilation lowering arterial CO₂.
explanation.a: Metabolic acidosis is not triggered by altitude exposure.
explanation.b: Metabolic alkalosis is not the primary response; it may occur later as compensation.
explanation.c: Respiratory acidosis results from hypoventilation, opposite of altitude physiology.
explanation.e: Mixed acid-base disorder is not typical in isolated altitude exposure.

subject: Physiology

statement: During acclimatization at high altitude, the change not likely to occur is?

explanation.d: Respiratory acidosis does not occur; hyperventilation causes alkalosis instead.
explanation.a: Accelerated erythropoiesis is a hallmark adaptation to hypoxia.
explanation.b: Increased hemoglobin concentration develops to improve oxygen carriage.
explanation.c: Increased rate of pulmonary ventilation is an immediate compensatory response.
explanation.e: Right ventricular hypertrophy can occur due to pulmonary hypertension at altitude.

subject: Physiology

statement: A navy worker remained in deep sea for about 8 hours and ascended rapidly to the surface. His symptoms are most likely due to:

options.a: exposure to atmospheric oxygen after surfacing.
options.b: formation of nitrogen bubbles in his body.
options.c: inhalation of a helium-rich breathing mixture.
options.d: low atmospheric pressure at the surface.

explanation.b: Rapid ascent lowers ambient pressure, causing dissolved nitrogen to form bubbles in tissues and blood, producing decompression sickness.
explanation.a: Exposure to atmospheric oxygen after surfacing does not cause decompression sickness.
explanation.c: Inhalation of a helium-rich breathing mixture reduces nitrogen-related decompression problems rather than causing them.
explanation.d: Low atmospheric pressure alone is not the direct mechanism; nitrogen bubble formation is responsible for symptoms.
explanation.e: Prolonged exposure to cold seawater may cause hypothermia but does not produce decompression sickness.

subject: Physiology

statement: Hyperbaric oxygen therapy is most effective in:

explanation.e: Hyperbaric oxygen therapy is particularly effective in gas gangrene because high oxygen tensions inhibit anaerobic bacterial growth and improve tissue oxygenation.
explanation.a: Anemic hypoxia is primarily due to reduced oxygen-carrying capacity and is not most effectively treated with hyperbaric oxygen therapy.
explanation.b: Carbon monoxide poisoning benefits from hyperbaric oxygen therapy, but gas gangrene is the condition in which it is considered most effective.
explanation.c: Chronic osteomyelitis may be treated adjunctively with hyperbaric oxygen therapy, but it is not the most effective indication.
explanation.d: Decompression sickness responds well to hyperbaric oxygen therapy, but gas gangrene represents a more definitive therapeutic indication.

subject: Physiology

statement: Hemoglobin is 89% saturated at:

explanation.d: At a partial pressure of 60 mmHg, the oxygen-hemoglobin dissociation curve flattens out, ensuring hemoglobin remains approximately 89% saturated.
explanation.a: At 21 mmHg, hemoglobin is highly unsaturated and falls well below its 50% saturation threshold.
explanation.b: At 28 mmHg, hemoglobin is only slightly above its P_{50} value and is roughly 55% saturated.
explanation.c: At 40 mmHg, which is typical of resting mixed venous blood, hemoglobin is approximately 75% saturated with oxygen.
explanation.e: At 68 mmHg, hemoglobin enters the upper plateau region of the curve where its saturation exceeds 92%.

statement: Dissociation of oxygen from oxyhemoglobin is facilitated by:

explanation.d: Exercise increases metabolic rate, which raises tissue temperature, PCO_2, and H^+ concentration, shifting the curve to the right to accelerate oxygen dissociation.
explanation.a: Decreased 2,3-diphosphoglycerate concentration shifts the curve to the left, which increases hemoglobin's affinity for oxygen and inhibits dissociation.
explanation.b: A decrease in H+ concentration raises pH and stabilizes the relaxed state of hemoglobin, reducing oxygen release.
explanation.c: Decreased temperature slows down molecular motion and stabilizes oxyhemoglobin, shifting the curve leftward to suppress dissociation.
explanation.e: Rest decreases metabolic demands and lowers heat and acid production, stabilizing oxygen binding rather than facilitating release.

statement: Oxygen-hemoglobin dissociation curve is shifted to the left by:

explanation.b: Fetal hemoglobin lacks the ability to bind 2,3-BPG effectively, giving it a higher oxygen affinity that shifts the dissociation curve to the left.
explanation.a: A fall in pH increases H^+ binding to hemoglobin, stabilizing the tense state and shifting the curve to the right.
explanation.c: Increased 2,3-diphosphoglycerate binds preferentially to deoxygenated hemoglobin, forcing a rightward shift to promote oxygen unloading.
explanation.d: Increased PCO2 enhances carbamino compound formation and hydrogen ion generation, driving a rightward shift via the Bohr effect.
explanation.e: Increased temperature weakens the iron-oxygen bonds, shifting the curve to the right to favor oxygen release to metabolically active tissues.

statement: What is the cause of left shift of oxygen-hemoglobin curve?

explanation.a: Carbon monoxide poisoning locks the remaining iron sites into a high-affinity state, preventing normal oxygen release and causing a structural left shift.
explanation.b: Exercise generates heat, lactic acid, and carbon dioxide, which structurally shifts the curve to the right to meet tissue metabolic demands.
explanation.c: Increased 2,3-BPG stabilizes the deoxygenated, tense conformation of hemoglobin, causing a distinct rightward shift.
explanation.d: Increased PCO2 enhances the Bohr effect by lowering intracellular pH, which induces a right shift in the dissociation curve.
explanation.e: Increased temperature breaks down the secondary bonds holding oxygen to heme, directly forcing a right shift.

statement: Increased oxygen displacing carbon dioxide from hemoglobin is known as the:

explanation.d: The Haldane effect dictates that oxygen binding to hemoglobin reduces its affinity for carbon dioxide and protons, promoting CO_2 unloading in the lungs.
explanation.a: The Bohr effect describes how increased carbon dioxide and hydrogen ions lower hemoglobin's affinity for oxygen at the tissue level.
explanation.b: The chloride shift is the reciprocal exchange of bicarbonate and chloride ions across the red blood cell membrane during gas transport.
explanation.c: The double Bohr effect is a specialized placental mechanism where reciprocal pH changes across maternal and fetal blood optimize oxygen transfer.
explanation.e: The Hamburger phenomenon is simply another historical clinical term for the chloride shift and does not describe oxygen-driven CO_2 displacement.

statement: Oxygen therapy is useless in which of the following case?

explanation.a: Anemic hypoxia is due to reduced hemoglobin concentration, so extra oxygen cannot increase oxygen content.
explanation.b: Fibrosis-related hypoxia improves with supplemental oxygen.
explanation.c: High altitude hypoxia responds to oxygen therapy.
explanation.d: Hypoventilation hypoxia benefits from oxygen supplementation.
explanation.e: V/Q defect hypoxia can be partially corrected with oxygen therapy.

statement: A child born with craniofacial defects and transposition of the great vessels most likely has abnormal development of:

explanation.e: Neural crest cells migrate extensively from the dorsal neural tube to form both the viscerocranium skeletal structures and the spiral aorticopulmonary septum; thus, their disruption causes paired craniofacial and outflow tract anomalies.
explanation.a: Standard surface ectoderm forms the epidermis and central nervous nervous tissue elements, but does not migrate to form the cardiac septa or facial bones.
explanation.b: The endoderm lines the epithelial tracts of the respiratory and gastrointestinal tracts, but does not differentiate into facial bones or outflow structures.
explanation.c: The hypoblast is an early blastocyst layer involved in establishing embryonic polarity and forming the yolk sac membrane, having no direct role in late organogenesis.
explanation.d: General mesoderm forms the myocardium and skeletal muscles, but defects strictly confined to the combination of facial bones and truncal septation point selectively to neural crest cell failure.

subject: Anatomy

statement: The ductus arteriosus persists after birth in part due to failure of oxygen-induced smooth muscle constriction. This smooth muscle originates embryologically from:

options.c: Neural crest–derived mesenchyme of the sixth arch

explanation.c: The vascular smooth muscle layer of the fourth and sixth aortic arches is uniquely composed of Neural crest–derived mesenchyme of the sixth arch, which mediates the critical postnatal contractile response to oxygen.
explanation.a: Endocardial cushion tissue is localized to the atrioventricular and conotruncal boundaries, contributing to valves and septa, not the great vessel media.
explanation.b: The mesothelium of the pericardial cavity forms the epicardium and visceral pericardium layers, not the media of the branchial arch arteries.
explanation.d: Somatic mesoderm of lateral plate forms the body wall structures and skeletal components, not the branchial arch vascular media.
explanation.e: Vitelline arterial mesenchyme forms the vascular wall components of abdominal vessels supplying the midgut loop.

subject: Anatomy

statement: A double aortic arch that forms a vascular ring around the trachea and esophagus results from persistence of:

options.a: both right and left fourth arch–dorsal aorta segments
options.b: left dorsal aorta between arches III and IV
options.c: right dorsal aorta distal to seventh intersegmental artery

explanation.a: A double aortic arch occurs when both right and left fourth arch–dorsal aorta segments persist, failure of the normal regression of the distal right dorsal aorta leads to a vascular ring surrounding the trachea and esophagus.
explanation.b: Abnormalities of the left dorsal aorta between arches III and IV typically disrupt the normal development of the common carotid and internal carotid system rather than forming a vascular ring.
explanation.c: Persistence or regression of the right dorsal aorta distal to seventh intersegmental artery is associated with an interrupted aortic arch or an aberrant right subclavian artery, not a double arch.
explanation.d: Persistence of the right sixth arch distal segment results in a right-sided ductus arteriosus, which does not independently encircle the trachea and esophagus as a double arch.
explanation.e: The ventral aortic sac contributes to the proximal ascending aorta and brachiocephalic trunk, and its abnormal partitioning does not cause the formation of a double aortic arch vascular ring.

subject: Anatomy

statement: During central venous catheterization through the left subclavian vein, a structure passing anterior to the root of the lung is accidentally injured. Which structure is most likely damaged?

explanation.a: The left phrenic nerve passes anterior to the root of the left lung (anterior to the lung hilum) as it descends to the diaphragm, placing it directly at risk during left subclavian venous catheterization.
explanation.b: The left recurrent laryngeal nerve loops under the aortic arch and ascends in the tracheoesophageal groove; it does not pass anterior to the lung root.
explanation.c: The left sympathetic trunk runs posterior to the lung root along the costovertebral junction, not anteriorly.
explanation.d: The left vagus nerve passes posterior to the root of the lung (not anterior), making it less vulnerable in this approach.
explanation.e: The right phrenic nerve is contralateral and entirely remote from a left subclavian approach.

subject: Histology

statement: Select incorrect match of anastomosis with its example:

options.a: anastomosis by convergence (Right and left vertebral arteries forming basilar artery)
options.b: end-to-end anastomosis (Right and left gastro-epiploic arteries)
options.c: lateral anastomosis (Anterior and posterior intercostal arteries)
options.e: transverse anastomosis (Ulnar and radial arteries at the wrist)

explanation.d: The central retinal arteries are strict anatomical end arteries with no collateral connections, making this a completely incorrect match for a potential anastomosis.
explanation.a: This is a correct match; the right and left vertebral arteries converge directly to form a single, larger vessel known as the basilar artery.
explanation.b: This is a correct match; the right and left gastro-epiploic arteries meet end-to-end along the greater curvature of the stomach.
explanation.c: This is a correct match; the anterior and posterior intercostal arteries run laterally along the rib spaces to form a functional side-to-side network.
explanation.e: This is a correct match; the ulnar and radial arteries connect via transverse arch networks across the wrist region.

subject: Histology

statement: Portal System exists in EXCEPT:

explanation.a: Emissary veins of the skull connect intracranial dural venous sinuses with extracranial veins to equalize pressure, but they do not form or connect two distinct capillary beds.
explanation.b: The renal system features an arterial portal system where the glomerular capillaries are connected directly to the peritubular capillaries via an efferent arteriole.
explanation.c: The hepatic portal system of the liver is the classic venous portal network, carrying nutrient-rich blood from the intestinal capillaries to the hepatic sinusoids.
explanation.d: The hypothalamo-hypophyseal system uses a portal network to carry hypothalamic regulatory hormones directly from the hypothalamus to the anterior pituitary gland.
explanation.e: The pancreatic acinar portal system links the islet capillaries directly to the acinar capillaries to deliver high concentrations of islet hormones to acinar cells.

subject: Histology

statement: A 77-year-old woman has a fainting episode. Echocardiography shows a 1-cm nodular lesion on the superior aspect of an intact anterior mitral valve leaflet and blood cultures are negative. Which of the following best describes this lesion:

explanation.d: A nodular valvular lesion attached to a valve leaflet is termed a vegetation.
explanation.a: Mural thrombi form on chamber walls rather than valve leaflets.
explanation.b: Myxoma is a cardiac tumor, usually arising in the atrium.
explanation.c: Phlebothrombosis refers to venous thrombosis.
explanation.e: Verruca is a specific type of vegetation seen in rheumatic disease.
